messages:
Elena (AE): Heads up — Aurora Financial wants a short POC next week to validate latency & burst behavior for their thin-client use case. Primary asks: 99th/99.9th latency under sustained 400 qps, 30s micro-bursts to 2k qps, and cost estimate for committed vs burst. Also they asked about cold-starts and encryption options.
Vikram (SRE): Got it. Proposed plan: steady-state run at 400 qps for 30m, then 3x 30s bursts to 2k qps spaced 5m apart, capture p50/p95/p99/p99.9 and tail CPU/GPU utilization. Warmup 10m with varying seq lengths (avg 64, 95th 256).
Amy (Sales Eng): For pricing attach, can we produce two numbers: committed monthly with reserved pool + 20% burst buffer, and fully on-demand burst pricing? Need rough $/1M tokens for both.
Vikram (SRE): Yes. For perf tests use dedicated pool config: model=redwood-v1-medium, batch_target=32, max_latency_slo=0.25s token (app-level). We'll use these load-test commands: ```bash
# k6 script run
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 30m aurora_400qps.js
# surge test
k6 run --vus 1000 --duration 30s aurora_burst.js
```
Vikram (SRE): Will enable prefix KV cache and mark 512 token max gen. Also capture KV cache hit rate.
Sam (Solutions): Aurora requires KMS/HSM at rest and in transit. For Private deployment they want HSM-backed keys. Can we confirm latency impact of HSM key unwrap on per-request path?
Vikram (SRE): HSM unwrap only impacts job start/credential refresh; request path uses session keys — negligible per-request latency. We'll include a cold-start test where a new container is provisioned and first request timing is measured (cold vs warm).
Elena (AE): They also want security questionnaire answers by EOD Tuesday. I'll send the list. Amy — can you produce the two pricing bullets by EOD Monday?
Amy (Sales Eng): Yep. I'll produce committed vs burst back-of-envelope and follow with a detailed spreadsheet.
Vikram (SRE): Test metrics we'll report: qps, p50/p95/p99/p99.9 of end-to-end latency, GPU utilization, batch sizes, KV cache hit rate, 5xx error rate, and token cost estimate derived from measured token/sec. Example report snip: ```
- Steady 400 qps: p99 = 210ms, p99.9 = 450ms, avg batch=27, cache_hit=72%, token_rate=1.3M/hr
- Burst 2k qps (30s): observed p99 = 1.2s, p99.9 = 2.6s, error_rate=0.3% (transient queue rejects)
```
sales_ops: Acceptance criteria from AE / CS: no more than 1% request errors during bursts, p99 < 500ms steady, documented mitigation for >500ms (fallback to smaller model).
sales_ops: Also need runbook steps for rapid rollback and model fallback during POC.
Sam (Solutions): For fallback: route policy -> redwood-v1-small (quantized) with lower cost, auto-fallback threshold p99>600ms or queue depth > 80%.
Elena (AE): Deployment windows: client prefers late-afternoon PST Tue. Vikram, can you own the run and we'd collectively review results Wed morning?
Vikram (SRE): I can own. Plan: provision dedicated pool 2h before test, run warmup, execute steady + bursts, then 1h soak. Will push logs and raw traces to shared GCS.
Elena (AE): Perfect.
deploy-bot: Deployment requested by @Vikram (SRE): dedicated-pool/aurora-test -> in_progress
deploy-bot: Provisioning nodes: 6/8 GPUs allocated, expected ready in ~12m :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Amy (Sales Eng): Quick question — for cost calc, do we include cold-start tax for infrequent invocations? Aurora said some endpoints are bursty and idle for hours.
Vikram (SRE): We'll include an amortized cold-start overhead metric (cost/hr for idle vs active) and show break-even point for reserved pool vs on-demand.
Elena (AE): Thanks team. I'll compile security Qs and acceptance criteria into a doc and share. Please add any extra metrics you want captured. :thumbsup:
Sam (Solutions): Add TLS 1.3 + mutual auth confirmation note.
Vikram (SRE): Adding collection of traces for first-byte times (cold) and steady-state tail latencies.
Elena (AE): Last ask — Aurora asked if we can simulate thin-client packetization: variable input sizes skewed small (avg 32 tokens) during bursts. Include that in load script.
Vikram (SRE): Will modify k6 script to sample from size distribution file. Also will include test seeds for reproducibility.
Amy (Sales Eng): I'll attach pricing spreadsheet and short slide for Monday.
Elena (AE): Great. Meeting scheduled Tue 17:00 PST. I'll send calendar invite.
